title: Establish progressive SLO experiment windows, tenant prioritization, and automated rollback heuristics
creator: Liam Chen
description: Create a product-level specification and acceptance criteria for staged SLO experiments that: 1) run in defined windows, 2) prioritize traffic by tenant class, and 3) include automated rollback heuristics tied to burn-rate and fidelity regressions. Goal is to enable controlled model and runtime changes without broad customer disruption and with clear escalation steps.
background: We frequently need to deploy model variants, quantized runtime builds, and routing changes. Current rollout gates are binary (canary or full) and do not support short experiment windows or tenant-aware prioritization. Engineering needs clear product requirements to implement short-lived experiments (15m, 1h, 6h), per-tenant progressive ramping, and deterministic auto-rollback triggers based on combined SLO and quality signals.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Product PRD describing three experiment window types (short:15m, medium:1h, extended:6h) and per-window traffic schedules. 2) Definition of three tenant classes (trial, standard, enterprise) with explicit traffic priorities and max allowed error-budget percentage consumption per window. 3) Concrete automated rollback rules: a) burn rate > 5x for 10m OR b) p99 latency regression > 30% vs baseline for 5m OR c) fidelity regression on canary prompt-set exceeding defined threshold. 4) Playbook pages (Confluence links) for manual override and escalation. 5) Wireframes for Console controls to launch experiment windows, set tenant priorities, and view real-time guard rails. 6) Integration acceptance tests (contract tests) defined for runtime to assert the rollback API is reachable and returns expected state transitions.
rollout_gates: - Probe: start with 0.5% traffic from 'trial' tenants for 15m. - Window progression: if metrics OK, expand to 2% over next 1h including 'standard' tenants. - Final ramp: after extended window (6h) and stable metrics, allow enterprise tenants and 100% rollout. - Hard stop gate: any single window with burn rate > 3x triggers immediate rollback to previous variant and notifies SRE and PM. - Quality gate: if prompt-set accuracy drop > 2% absolute, halt and rollback immediately.
monitoring_and_signals: Primary signals: p50/p95/p99 latency, request error rate, token-level cost delta, SLO burn rate, and fidelity checks on a fixed probe prompt-set. Secondary signals: CPU/GPU stalls, queue length, memory OOMs, and model output degradation alerts from eval service. Dashboards: per-window dashboard showing rolling 1m/5m/15m burn rate and a canary health score (0-100). Alerts: page at SEV-1 for burn rate > 5x sustained 10m and SEV-2 for p99 > 2x baseline for 15m.
decisions: Use tenant classification (trial/standard/enterprise) as primary ramping axis rather than per-tenant manual selection
Automated rollback will be enacted by runtime via an idempotent rollback API; UI can trigger but not required for safety
Fidelity probes are defined as a fixed set of 200 prompts maintained in the eval repo; threshold set at 2% absolute drop for initial implementation
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: false positives in fidelity probes causing unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: run three consecutive 1m checks before auto-rollback and require at least one corroborating infra signal (e.g., high queue length). Risk: enterprise customer impact during progressive ramp. Mitigation: exclude flagged enterprise tenants from first two windows by default and provide a manual opt-in flow.
notes: Align with SRE on burn-rate computation to ensure it matches billing metrics
Design to prototype Console controls in next design sprint
Product will own PRD + acceptance criteria; Engineering owns runtime enforcement and tests
next_steps: 1) Review PRD draft with SRE and Runtime (by 2025-10-20). 2) Design Console UX mockups (design sprint 2025-W42). 3) Engineering spike to implement rollback API contract and test harness (ENG spike Q4 week). 4) Schedule a dry-run internal experiment with synthetic traffic before any customer-facing ramp.
qa_and_test_plan: Define contract tests that simulate spike in burn-rate, latency regressions, and fidelity degradation. Tests must assert rollback is triggered and that metrics return to baseline. Include a chaos scenario where rollback API is temporarily unreachable to validate manual mitigation steps.
communication_plan: Notify customers via status page for any experiments that include non-excluded tenants. Prepare a one-pager for account owners of enterprise tenants explaining opt-in flow. Internal runbook updates and on-call playbook to be distributed to SRE and Support.
closure_criteria: PRD approved by SRE and Runtime leads, Console mockups reviewed by Design, rollback API implemented and covered by automated tests, and a successful internal dry-run with no unresolved SEV incidents.
